Under ZDR (body flag or the token's floor) the cache is neither read nor written and no key is computed, not even a hashed URL (a hash of a known URL is a membership oracle); the scrape runs as a fresh fetch and the response carries the warning max_age_ignored_zdr with cache_state bypass. job_results_routes::gate refuses a caller whose token floor is ZDR before it asks Control Plane anything: a row is the URL, title and artifact ids of a page the job fetched (INNH-12), read from control's page_fetched events. Dark behind QUARRY_EDGE__JOB_RESULTS (501 off, which wins over the refusal); a service principal is refused 403 by the route scope. No ZDR job exists to have results (crawl and batch are refused at handoff) and a ZDR run stores no artifact, so the ids are absent for it as well. Page content is not in the response: it is read by id through the artifacts row, which binds the read to the org

webhook_subscription_routes::gate refuses create, patch and delivery retry for a caller whose token floor is ZDR before it asks Control Plane anything (403, details.reason webhook_off_process): a subscription pushes the page URL and fingerprints of every detected change to a third party. Reads, delete and secret rotation stay open so a ZDR organization can wind down what it holds. Dark behind QUARRY_EDGE__WEBHOOK_SUBSCRIPTIONS (501 off, which wins over the refusal); a service principal is refused 403 by the route scope and by the gate. Nothing is sent for a ZDR run in any case: emit_change_side_effects suppresses the change event and webhook for a declared zdr, so a subscription an organization made before it turned ZDR receives nothing from a ZDR check. Control keeps a subscription (URL and the HMAC secret, the secret stored in plaintext: see the owner decision in docs/RUNBOOKS.md) and each delivery row (the event payload) until delete, org erasure or the delivery retention sweep (default 14 days)

The orchestrator declares the posture quarry-control stamped on the schedule at create (migration 023); a schedule created before that (NULL) or before its org turned ZDR on declares nothing or false and is stored (pinned by zdr_posture_stamp::record_trusts_the_stamp_not_the_current_posture); the orchestrator also declares the stamp on the run_page fetch that precedes the record call, so a stamped-ZDR monitor's fetch runs in ZDR mode and persists no page artifact, event or local-index write-back; ChangeMonitorWF still emits run_started and change_detected with the URL.
